intro.title: Active Listening
paragraphs: You are a new employee of a financial company. After sorting out the initial matters, you have been invited to participate in the internal development program. The main focus of this program is the enhancement of the skill of Active Listening among the company's staff.
As you arrive to the workplace, you are told that the training has an individual character, and you will be invited on the rooftop, where the training is taking place, when your time comes.

You're excited about it, and you are hoping that this upskill program will really turn out to be effective. To unlock the skill of active listening you need to successfully accomplish the training prepared for you by the company.

dialogues.greet: Good morning! It's really nice to meet you. Let me start from the short explanation of today's activities. You will be tasked with solving three different exercises, each one focusing on the development of your ability of active listening. Before each of them, you will have to find a piece of theoretical knowledge hidden somewhere around, enabling you to successfully complete the exercise. Sounds simple, right? Let's get to it then!
dialogues.clue:
We will start with basics. Somewhere around this area, we have hidden the first piece of knowledge, that you will need to familiarize yourself with. We have for you this clue, which should help you find it:

"Not on the bench, not on the floor -
where plants grow tall, there's something more"

Are you ready? Let the search begin!
dialogues.fastLearner: Oh, you have found that document very fast, well done! Now, as our first exercise, let's test your newly gained knowledge! Take a look at the laptop.
dialogues.puzzle1Done: Exactly! You're a fast learner! Now, before we will move on to the next task, I would like to… Hm, what is it, Zainabu?
dialogues.interrupted: *Mateo gets interrupted, as Zainabu is trying to tell him something. He's turning to her, she starts talking to him.*
dialogues.backToYou: Anyway, I'm sorry for that. I do believe we are ready for the next exercise, right? It's already displayed for you on the laptop. Let's take a look.
dialogues.congratsFinal: That's true. It was really impressive! You have mastered the skill of active listening and passed our tests with flying colors! You set the bar really high - the next participants will have a really tough time trying to beat your score! Thank you once again for your time and effort.
dialogues.default: I'm here if you need me.

dialogues.conv1: I'm sorry to interrupt, but this is important. Did you review the updated risk report template that came in this morning?
dialogues.conv3: I noticed that the specific values are grouped differently now, especially in the risk section, and I wasn't sure if that changes how we calculate the quarterly summaries.
dialogues.conv5: Alright. What made me worry was that the comparison table no longer shows the same totals as last quarter.
dialogues.conv7: Let me check if I understand you correctly. From your perspective, the calculations stay the same and only the presentation has changed?
dialogues.conv9: That's helpful to clarify. In that case, maybe we should verify it before sending the final report.
dialogues.pendriveTask: You're a really good listener yourself, you know. You have done very well with this last assignment. But we have one more task ahead of you, before we consider this training completed. Somewhere around here we have hidden a pendrive. On that pendrive, there is the last piece of knowledge that you need to solve your last task. It's a red pendrive. Let me know once you find it!
dialogues.readyForFinal: Yes. Now you're ready to face the final challenge. Go ahead and click on the laptop, whenever you're ready.
dialogues.congratsFinal: This is it! You're fully correct! It's not your first active listening training, is it? You have done really well today. You have managed to not only quickly learn from our materials, but also perfectly recognize and understand all the live cues that we have prepared for you!
dialogues.completion: It was a pleasure working with you today!

dialogues.conv2: Not in detail. I assumed it's the same as before, just a standard update.
dialogues.conv4: I don't think so. These updates are usually cosmetic. We've had similar ones before.
dialogues.conv6: It's probably fine. If compliance changed the layout, the numbers themselves should still be correct.
dialogues.conv8: Yes, that's what I mean. But now that you mention the totals, I realize I haven't actually confirmed it.
dialogues.conv10: You're right. I'll check the calculation rules and confirm with compliance before we submit anything.

multiChoice.title: Understanding the Basics
multiChoice.question: Which behaviors are examples of active listening?

options.a: Thinking ahead about how to respond while the other person speaks.
options.b: Allowing pauses and moments of silence without interrupting.
options.c: Focusing mainly on reaching agreement as quickly as possible.
options.d: Paying attention to the speaker's words, tone, and body language.

multiChoice.hint: Remember that an important part of active listening is respecting your interlocutor and what they're saying.

feedback.wrong: That's not quite right. Remember that active listening is about respecting your interlocutor and what they're saying.
feedback.correct: Well done! Those are the correct examples of active listening.

multiChoice.answerOverlay:
The correct answers are:
• Allowing pauses and moments of silence without interrupting.
• Paying attention to the speaker's words, tone, and body language.

popupContent: Active listening means being fully present in a conversation. It is not about waiting for your turn to speak or thinking about what you will say next while the other person is talking.

When you listen actively, your attention is focused on the speaker only, without distractions or interruptions. You notice not only the words being spoken, but also other characteristics, such as tone of voice, pauses, and body language, allowing you to understand the message more completely.
The purpose of active listening is understanding, not agreement. It involves giving the speaker time, allowing silence when it appears, and responding only after the message has been fully received.

When people feel listened to in such a way, they are more likely to feel respected, understood, and willing to communicate openly. Active listening helps reduce misunderstandings, improves trust, and supports better cooperation in everyday work interactions.
Active listening includes managing your own reactions so they don't interrupt the understanding of the message.
Good listeners notice changes in tone or pace as signals that meaning may be changing.
Listening well sometimes means not responding immediately, even when you know what you want to say.
Paraphrasing is most effective when it captures meaning, not exact words.
Active listening helps prevent escalation by slowing conversations before emotions rise.
Being listened to often helps the speaker clarify their own thinking, even without feedback.
